answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4, and draws 2 Final Scoring cards. Put the Animals Action card in the leftmost slot (strength 1); place the other four randomly in the remaining slots. All five start side I up. Starting Appeal is staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1: Appeal track staggered 0/1/2/3 by turn order; C3: 1 worker on notepad and 3 lying down; D: take 25 money; E: draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: draw 8, keep 4. Setup B: Animals under leftmost slot, remaining 4 randomly; side I up.

answers.answer: Place 4 face-up Base Conservation Projects in a four-player game and 3 in a two- or three-player game. Only in a two-player game, block the left level on the left face-up project, the middle level on the middle project, and the right level on the right project; also block the three spaces in the left donation-area column. No such blocking is specified for three or four players. Reveal the six-card display after all players have chosen their hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: 4 projects in a 4-player game; otherwise 3. Setup 5c: 2-player-only blocked levels and donation spaces. Personal setup G: reveal the display after everyone has chosen hand cards.

answers.answer: After using a card from slot 4, remove it; shift cards that were to its left one slot right, then put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent beforehand adds 1 strength, while X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that action. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. Resolve an effect marked “after finishing” after completing the action and moving its Action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card from its slot, shift cards left of the empty slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. X-tokens: set strength before acting; maximum 5. “After finishing” effects occur after moving the Action cards.

answers.answer: You may not do nothing as a regular action; playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal. The alternative X-token action gives exactly 1 X-token and still requires selecting an Action card, moving it to slot 1, and shifting intervening cards right. Slot strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action when you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “You may not do nothing.” X-token action: take exactly 1, move the selected card to slot 1, and its strength/upgrade state are irrelevant; unavailable at 5 held.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore extra steps and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. Finish the current turn, then take the break. After the break the Break token resets to the player-count starting space, and play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: “the break takes place after the end of your current turn,” gain 1 X-token, and ignore steps beyond the last space. Break procedure step 6: reset the token; play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: On Cards I, advance the Break token 2 spaces without money, then either draw the amount shown for the action strength (maximum 3) and make any required discard, or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation with no deck draw. On Cards II, also advance 2 spaces, then draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order using the upgraded table; a snap is available from strength 3 and still takes exactly 1 card of any reputation with no deck draw. Reputation restriction applies only to the Cards II draw option. Display cards taken are replenished after the entire turn. Hand limit is enforced only at breaks, not during play.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces; I snap at strength 5+, II at 3; snapping is exactly one unrestricted display card, and reputation restriction applies only to the II draw option. Display refills at turn end; hand limit is checked only at breaks.

answers.answer: “Within reputation range” includes the display folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. Above reputation 15, the counter stays at 15 and each additional reputation step gives 1 Appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: range is the matching folder plus lower-numbered folders; 10+ requires Cards II; at 15 further reputation gives 1 Appeal per step; “You may not look through the discard pile.”

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building, with size no greater than action strength. Build II can build different buildings whose total size is at most the strength, but not two identical buildings in the same action. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, cannot extend beyond the map or cover water/rock, and restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion gives 1 Appeal immediately, once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: I builds exactly 1; II builds different buildings up to total strength; cost is 2 money per space. Placement rules give first-building border placement, later adjacency, restricted spaces, and kiosk spacing. Pavilion increases Appeal by 1.

answers.answer: Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II additionally allows a Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary. Each special-enclosure type has four supply tiles, and each individual zoo can have only one of each type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 Appeal.
answers.evidence: Buildings table and Build description: Petting Zoo is available on I; Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary on II; four tiles of each special enclosure and one of each per zoo. Unique buildings only enter through Sponsor cards. Full map grants 7 Appeal.

answers.answer: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. Ordinary effects resolve immediately; effects marked “after finishing” wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses the order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens: earlier action bonuses may be used for later steps, resolve items one at a time, and pay before own benefits. “After finishing” effects follow action completion and card movement. Simultaneous effects: owning player chooses order.

answers.answer: For each animal, meet all card conditions, pay its cost, and provide legal housing. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces the cost by 3 money per continent icon, so two matching icons reduce it by 6. Standard housing requires one empty standard enclosure at least the printed size; flip the whole enclosure to its occupied side, and it normally houses one animal. Petting Zoo animals can only use the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may use their indicated special enclosure instead, using player tokens for the animal's indicated number of spaces; special enclosures are never flipped. Required water/rock adjacency applies to standard or chosen special housing and counts distinct adjacent hexes. Animal effects normally resolve as each animal is played; “after finishing” effects wait until the Animals action is complete and its card has moved.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: check conditions and pay cost; matching partner zoo discount is 3 per continent icon. Enclosure-state table says flip standard enclosure; place tokens on special enclosure and never flip. Animal admission describes terrain adjacency and effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II allows Animal cards from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; each display animal costs an additional amount equal to its folder number. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the expanded range is available for that action. The display is not replenished until the turn ends. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS Side II: play from display within range, pay folder number, and at strength 5+ gain reputation at the very beginning; display replenishes at turn end; upgrade-required conditions are allowed.

answers.answer: Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, you may move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, deciding separately for each; check terrain adjacency and available capacity. Mark each moved animal's indicated number of special-enclosure spaces with your supply player tokens. For each animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size requirement, flip none. This relocation is once per building and is distinct from releasing an animal.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals section: allowed only immediately when the new special enclosure is built; move all suitable animals that fit, separately; add indicated tokens; free the smallest standard enclosure meeting all requirements, with size-only and no-enclosure fallbacks.

answers.answer: Association task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, and conservation-project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task, needs at least one active worker, and action strength must meet the task strength. If one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers; if 3 are there, you cannot do it again before the break. Other players' workers do not matter. Association II performs one or more different tasks, using 1 or 2 of your workers per task, with total task value no greater than action strength.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION: task strengths are listed as 2/3/4/5. Side I specifies active worker and repeat-task worker rules, and says other players' workers do not matter. Side II permits different tasks within total strength.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them in the lowest empty matching space on your map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and take printed university reputation when acquired. You cannot acquire a duplicate university. Partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4; the third and fourth require Association II. Universities are the only way to raise hand limit from 3 to 5, and only the hand-limit university does so. The board is replenished at breaks so each tile is available once, skipping tiles all players already have.
answers.evidence: Association tasks: gain zoo/university from Association board into lowest space, take printed bonus, no duplicate university, and partner restrictions. University table gives hand-limit effect. Break procedure replenishes partner zoos and universities exactly once.

answers.answer: Association I can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also play a new project from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. A support requires a fulfilled condition with no player token on it; each reward level holds one token total, and you normally support a particular project only once. Take the support token from your zoo-map left edge. Removing it activates its map bonus immediately, which you may take before or after the project reward. New projects go in the leftmost space above the Association board and push others right; if this exceeds the player-count limit (2, 3, or 4 projects), discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies, while their map bonuses stay activated. Base projects below the board do not move.
answers.evidence: Association project work and support rules: new card from hand or display on II, unoccupied reward conditions, one token per level and usual once-per-project limit; take token from left map edge and choose bonus timing. Overflow rule returns tokens to supply; base projects never move.

answers.answer: The Release into the Wild category is determined by the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. First lose only the animal's printed Appeal, then discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated Appeal, and effects already earned. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free housing, if the animal could live in a special enclosure, first remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone as fallback; if none meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects: exact size-category mapping; lose printed Appeal before conservation, discard animal/icons, retain other listed gains, and new-project reputation. Special tokens/standard-enclosure release and fallback procedure are specified.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand when action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II plays one or more cards from hand or from the display within reputation range, paying the display folder number; action strength plus 1 must cover the sum of card levels. Resolve cards one after another, fully resolving each card's instant effects except “after finishing” effects before the next. If using Sponsors I to advance the Break token instead, advance by action strength and take that much money even if fewer steps remain before the last space. The Sponsors II break option pays twice the money.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: side-I level/hand limit and break money even if token needs fewer steps; side-II strength+1 level budget, display cost, sequence, and double-money break option.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens; return workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down, and refill; take income (Appeal-track money, kiosk income, then break-income Sponsor/map effects); reset the Break token. The hand limit is normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. If several players receive display cards during income, resolve those players clockwise starting from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 give order and hand limit. Kiosk income lists qualifying neighbors. The income/display paragraph specifies clockwise order and refill after each affected player's income.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an additional association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus token. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before scoring. Check the game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn ends or a break, unless another player triggers the end first. If triggered at the end of a turn, the triggering player finishes and each other player gets one more turn; if triggered during a break, everyone gets one more turn. A Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with the most supported conservation projects, then tied players share the win.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: milestone rewards at 2, 5/8, and 10; end check timing and last turns; Final Scoring card cap; VP formula and project-support tiebreak.
